v1_problem: CRM dispute tickets roughly doubled from a ~600/month baseline in Jun-Jul to 1180 (Aug) and 1260 (Sep) 2026 (E-04); a manual-read route-completion shortfall (88% vs 95% target, 9200 accounts, Aug-Sep, E-05) — coincident with the field reader staffing gap reported since July — drove increased estimate substitution that accounts for the ESTIMATED-read 41% share of disputed bills (1240/3025, E-01). This field-read mechanism does not explain the ACTUAL-read majority (59%) of disputes, since slow response handling (rejected, E-03) and a tariff change (rejected, E-02) have both been ruled out as causes.
v2_problem: CRM dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from a ~600/month baseline (Jun-Jul 2026) to 1180 (Aug) and 1260 (Sep) 2026 (E-04). Of disputed bills, 1240 (41%) carry an ESTIMATED read type (E-01); E-12 shows 1184 of these (95%) had a valid, timely AMI read exported to billing but rejected at import with status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, not a missing/lost read. E-13 shows validation rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01, compares the raw cumulative register value directly against 12-month m3 consumption history with no unit scaling, and E-14 shows firmware v4.2 meters (rolled out 2026-06) record registers in units of 0.1 m3 versus legacy plain m3 — a 10x magnitude mismatch that would cause BV-17's unscaled comparison to misflag normal v4.2 usage as high-consumption, forcing estimate substitution. This billing-import rule defect explains the mechanism producing most ESTIMATED-read disputed bills; it does not establish the cause of the ACTUAL-read majority (59%, 1785 bills) of disputes, which remains unattributed.
